podcast.body: A hugely important and "grandísimo" track released in 1982-1983, "Planet Rock" is considered a key pillar of hip hop music, known for its groundbreaking sound and influence. "82 83 sale el grandísimo plan en rock de africa bambata."

podcast.body: In the Bronx, Afrika Bambaataa combined a Roland TR-808 drum machine with evocative melodies from Kraftwerk's "Trans-Europe Express" to create "Planet Rock." This track is recognized as a foundational piece of electro music and a pillar of hip-hop. "África van batada a la Báser en Ambers, a una Roll-Anterrey 808, y le metió las evocadoras melodías de transduropexpress para crear Planet Rock, el tema afundacional del electro, ya sabéis, uno de los pilares del gig-hop."

podcast.body: This all-time hip hop classic from 1982 by Afrika Bambaataa heavily utilized and was directly influenced by the beats from Kraftwerk's 1977 album "Trans-Europe Express." It serves as a prime example of how Kraftwerk's sound laid the foundation for hip hop. "The track is Planet Rock and it's an all-time hip hop classic."

podcast.body: This seminal track is identified as one of the absolute musical pillars for all electronic music made in the United States, including modern Hip Hop, Techno, and House music. It was heavily influenced by German electronic music, specifically Kraftwerk, from whom it directly sampled musical fragments. "su grandísimo hip planet rock que es uno de los pilares de toda la música electrónica que se hizo en estados unidos del hip hop moderno y de la música tecnota de la música House, uno de los pilares musicales absolutos en estados unidos es planet rock."

podcast.body: This track, released by New York DJ and MC Afrika Bambaataa, is considered "Ground Zero" for a multitude of electronic dance music genres, including house, electro, garage, and Miami bass. It also had a profound impact on the future of hip hop, notably featuring a sample from Kraftwerk's "Trans-Europe Express." "In 1982, a New York DJ and MC named Africa Bumbata released a track called Planet Rock. And this one song became Ground Zero, the source of everything from house to electro, garage and Miami bass."
